title: Can one short rule give the bill for any laddu order?
description: A sweet shop gets a different order of coconuts and jaggery every day. A photo opens the video, two order cards follow, and it stops on the question of one short way to say the bill, with no answer shown.
teaching_notes: One idea: the way the bill is worked out stays fixed while the amounts change. Ask each child to say the rule in their own words and do not confirm any wording, because the next topic builds it. Watch for students who think each new order needs a new method.

video_script.why: Before any letter is used, the child meets the real need: one short way to say how every bill is worked out, however the order changes.
video_script.substitution: Picture each order as a card of coconuts and jaggery, and the bill as the same working applied to different numbers.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_2}}'s sweet shop gets a different order every day, but the bill is worked out the same way each time
never_show: any letter standing for a number
the price of a coconut or of a kilogram of jaggery
maths_rules: The bill is the cost of the coconuts plus the cost of the jaggery.
The way of working out the bill is the same every day; only the amounts change.
The open question: how to write that one way for any order. No letter and no formula is shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: a fixed way of working with changing amounts. Assumes nothing. Wrong idea: none is broken. The photo sits as a dimmed backdrop in the first beat and fades before the order cards arrive; the cards stay to the end.
